name: Saint Justin Martyr
history: A philosopher from Samaria who searched the schools of the Greeks for the truth and found it in Christ. He kept his philosopher’s cloak and opened a school in Rome, where he defended the faith in writing before the emperor. His account of a Sunday Mass is the earliest we have. He was beheaded for refusing to sacrifice to the gods.
life: Justin was born of pagan parents at Flavia Neapolis, the modern Nablus. He tried the Stoics, a follower of Aristotle, a Pythagorean and the Platonists in turn. By his own account an old man he met walking by the sea told him of the prophets, who had spoken of Christ long before, and a fire was kindled in his soul. Baptised, he taught in Rome as a Christian philosopher. His First Apology, addressed to the Emperor Antoninus Pius, describes how Christians gathered on the day of the sun, read the memoirs of the apostles, prayed, and received bread and wine which they believed to be the flesh and blood of Jesus. His Dialogue with Trypho records a long, courteous debate with a Jew. Around 165 he and six companions were tried before the prefect Rusticus, and the record of their trial survives.
prayerTo: Saint Justin, you sought the truth with all your mind and gave your life when you had found it. Pray for all who study and search, for teachers and for those who doubt. Help me to give a reason for the hope that is in me, with gentleness and courage, and to love the Mass you described so faithfully. Amen.
penance: Read a page of Scripture or of a Father of the Church slowly today, and give some time to explaining your faith kindly to someone who asks.
meditation: Justin held that every seed of truth in the philosophers belonged to Christ, the Word. Where have you seen a seed of His truth in someone who does not yet know Him?
